headlines.title: THE MARKETS: STOCKS; Another Sell-Off in Technology Sends Nasdaq Into a Correction
headlines.abstract: Nasdaq composite index finishes down 186.78 points, or 4 percent, to 4,457.89, fifth-largest point decline ever for Nasdaq; index is down 11.7 percent from peak of 5,048.62 it set less than three weeks ago; slide surpasses 10 percent, benchmark Wall Street uses to define a correction; Dow Jones industrial average drops 38.47 points, or 0.35 percent, to 10,980.25, after being up as much as 125 points; Standard & Poor's 500-stock index drops 20.60 points, or 1.4 percent, to 1,487.92; graphs; charts; photo (M)

headlines.title: THE MARKETS: STOCKS & BONDS; Another Sell-Off in Technology Pushes Nasdaq Into Bear Market
headlines.abstract: Nasdaq composite index drops 7.06 percent, or 286.27 points, to 3,769.63; slide is sixth largest in percentage terms and second largest in points in index's history; Nasdaq has fallen 25.3 percent from its peak on March 10, sinking into territory of 20 percent or greater retreat that Wall Street designates as bear market; Dow Jones industrial average closes down 161.95 points, at 11,125.13; Standard & Poor's 500-stock index plummets 33.42 points, to 1,467.17; graph; chart; photo (M)

headlines.title: THE MARKETS: STOCKS & BONDS; Nasdaq Gasps for Air, Then Faints Away Again, by 2.5%
headlines.abstract: Nasdaq composite index drops 92.85 points, or 2.5 percent, at 3,676.78; index is 27.2 percent below its March 10 peak, firmly in what is regarded as bear-market territory; Dow Jones industrial average drops 201.58 points, or 1.8 percent, to 10,923.55; Standard & Poor's 500-stock index falls 26.66 points, or 1.82 percent, to 1,440.51; graph; chart (M)
